record.title: Soei preprint reports a single-developer audit of coding-agent evidence and history
record.summary: An Oct. 29 arXiv preprint presents Soei, a provenance and verification observability design, alongside a prototype study of 45 real VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer. The authors report 102,233 records and 20,577 tool executions. Their audited rule-based classifier yields a bias-corrected estimate that 23.4% of code-editing episodes ended without an independent check after the last edit (95% CI 17.1–35.7); 57.8% of edit-backed to-dos marked complete had no recorded proof between the last edit and completion. The authors also report that their content-free, hash-chained ledger occupied about 20% of the raw transcript size and detected a tamper test. The private corpus is not released. These are author-reported single-user pilot findings, not population estimates or evidence that a classified check establishes correctness.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report analyzing 45 real VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer, spanning 23 April to 5 October 2026, with 102,233 transcript records and 20,577 tool executions. The source corpus is private and was not inspected here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Using their final audited rule-based classifier, the authors report a bias-corrected estimate that 23.4% of code-editing episodes ended without a recorded independent check after the last edit (95% CI 17.1–35.7). This describes the paper's corpus and classifier, not population prevalence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 186 of 322 edit-backed to-dos (57.8%) marked complete had no recorded verification between the last code edit and the completion status. Their definition of verification includes execution and UI checks, not only formal tests.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the same corpus, the authors report a content-free hash-chained ledger at about 20% of raw transcript size, deterministic replay and detection of a tamper test. No independent implementation or performance reproduction was conducted here.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that the reported rates generalize to other developers, agent products or work domains; that its verification label implies correctness; or that displaying the proposed evidence changes supervisor decisions. The private source corpus is not released.

evidence_gaps.description: The study uses one developer's VS Code Copilot session corpus. No independent multi-developer replication was found; the authors frame it as a pilot rather than a population estimate.
The paper describes prototype scripts and frozen aggregate artifacts, but this review did not run the prototype or reproduce ledger size, throughput, classification or tamper-detection results.
A recorded independent check is not equivalent to correctness, and the paper does not measure whether its proposed interface improves supervisory decisions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the observed gaps and low-cost evidence-ledger prototype generalize, coding-agent completion displays and durable history could be designed around independently checked evidence rather than agent-reported status. The empirical corpus is one developer using one VS Code agent product, so population prevalence and broader operational effects are not established.
limitations: The corpus contains 45 sessions from one developer and one VS Code Copilot agent-mode product; findings do not establish population prevalence.
The proof classifier is rule-based. Its final precision audit sampled 30 episodes per label, and the reported estimate is sensitive to the classifier version and definition of verification.
The authors define verification as an independent check after the last edit; this does not establish that the change is correct.
The session corpus is private and was not released; no independent replication of empirical or prototype results was performed here.
brief.summary: An Oct. 29 arXiv preprint presents Soei, a provenance and verification observability design, alongside a prototype study of 45 real VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer. The authors report 102,233 records and 20,577 tool executions. Their audited rule-based classifier yields a bias-corrected estimate that 23.4% of code-editing episodes ended without an independent check after the last edit (95% CI 17.1–35.7); 57.8% of edit-backed to-dos marked complete had no recorded proof between the last edit and completion. The authors also report that their content-free, hash-chained ledger occupied about 20% of the raw transcript size and detected a tamper test. The private corpus is not released. These are author-reported single-user pilot findings, not population estimates or evidence that a classified check establishes correctness.

technical.claimed_result: On 45 VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer, the authors report 23.4% of code-edit episodes ended without a recorded independent check after the last edit (bias-corrected 95% CI 17.1–35.7), and 186/322 edit-backed completed to-dos (57.8%) had no proof action between edit and completion. These are corpus- and classifier-specific author-reported results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1.2 preprint and its methods, tables and limitations were inspected. No private source transcripts were accessed and no prototype execution, independent labeling or replication was performed in this review.
technical.mechanism: Soei proposes normalized events with acknowledgement states, a local append-only hash-chained ledger, an evidence graph and a verifier that separates reported completion from observed proof. The authors' pilot prototype folds logged events into artifact lineage and applies a versioned rule-based classifier; this review did not run the prototype.
technical.regime: One developer's real VS Code Copilot agent-mode session history from April–October 2026: 45 sessions, 102,233 raw records, 20,577 tool executions and 2,336 human-to-agent episodes. This is a private single-user corpus; other agent products, users and domains were not studied.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes a standard-library-only prototype, frozen aggregate results, figure scripts and audit sheets. The source corpus is withheld because it is the authors' private work history and contains sensitive material. This review did not execute the artifacts or independently reproduce reported results.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within the paper, the authors compare four successive classifier versions and report blind audits of 30 episodes per sampled label; the unverified rate shifts from 42.1% in v1 to 25.1% in v4, then to an audit-corrected 23.4% estimate. No independent team baseline was inspected.

brief.title: Soei preprint reports a single-developer audit of coding-agent evidence and history
brief.why_it_matters: If replicated across developers and agent products, evidence linked to artifact versions could help supervisors distinguish an agent's completion claim from a check that actually ran. The study provides a concrete measurement and prototype in one person's workflow, but does not establish prevalence across teams or that the proposed system improves human decisions.
